headline: LRMoE reports faster memory-constrained training for two sparse MoE models
summary: A preprint introduces LRMoE, which selects backward token–expert contributions using a local gradient-impact score, plans expert placement under memory and communication constraints, then compacts retained rows before communication and grouped GEMMs. On eight Hopper GPUs with an 80 GiB per-GPU budget, the authors report 21.2–44.8% lower cumulative MoE-layer time to four matched loss targets than SYMI for Qwen3-30B-A3B and GLM4.5-106B-A12B, despite additional training steps. These are author-reported results on two configurations and a locally reused Alpaca corpus; they exclude non-MoE layers and are not whole-model end-to-end savings. The appendix proves optimality only for a fixed-count, equal-row-cost additive sum of isolated projection-gradient perturbations. No independent reproduction was performed.
